summary: Owned units s0222–s0243 contain no births or ages. The only deaths are 獻之卒 (s0239) and 月餘亦卒 (s0241); both are claimed. Zuo Si, Jing Dan, and Sima Xiangru appear only as later reception and are correctly kept off life dates, with empty active hints. Dai Kui’s presence in 剡 and the night reading are source-undated. Wang Huizhi’s Palace Attendant tenure, resignation, and the 俱病篤 sentence likewise give no year. Xianzhi’s illness and death are dated from 及安薨 plus 未幾／俄而. Jin Shu Xiaowu annals place Xie An’s death on 東晉孝武帝太元十年八月丁酉, distinct from the earlier Wu 太元 era. Calendar tables equate that eighth-month day with AD 385 (Julian witness 10-12; proleptic Gregorian remains AD 385, not a New-Year-edge case). The 385–386 window for Xianzhi and the one-sided onOrAfter AD 385 bound for Huizhi’s death are therefore supported. hints-p083 is incorrect: it feeds Huizhi’s death into active-date-hints, which must stay separate from activity.

itemChecks.event: Dai Kui was in Shan when Wang Huizhi thought of him and travelled by night.
itemChecks.reason: Owner is Dai Kui (p078). s0229–s0230 say 忽憶戴逵 and 逵時在剡 during Huizhi’s snowy-night boat trip. No reign year, month, or day is given, so the undated attestation is the correct endpoint treatment. This is Dai Kui’s own presence, not a later quotation of him.

itemChecks.event: Wang Xianzhi read the Gao Shi Zhuan Zan at night with Wang Huizhi and praised Jing Dan.
itemChecks.reason: Owner is Wang Xianzhi in this anecdote (p079). s0232 records 嘗夜與弟獻之共讀《高士傳贊》，獻之賞井丹高潔. 嘗夜 supplies no calendar year. The claim correctly leaves the reading undated and does not borrow Xie An’s later death year.

evidence.quote: 嘗夜與弟獻之共讀《高士傳贊》，獻之賞井丹高潔

itemChecks.event: Dai Kui was in Shan during Wang Huizhi’s overnight boat journey.
itemChecks.reason: Owner is Dai Kui (p078). 逵時在剡 is a place-association for that visit. 時在 states location, not a reign year, so undated resided-at/stay is justified. No second endpoint is invented.

evidence.quote: 逵時在剡，便夜乘小船詣之

itemChecks.event: Wang Huizhi later held office as Palace Attendant.
itemChecks.reason: Owner is Wang Huizhi (p083). s0235 後為黃門侍郎 is his own office in narrative sequence after the undated anecdotes. 後為 is relative order only; no year is stated, so undatedSourceAttestation is the justified endpoint.

itemChecks.event: Wang Huizhi resigned as Palace Attendant and returned east.
itemChecks.reason: Owner is Wang Huizhi (p083). The same sentence continues 棄官東歸 after 後為黃門侍郎. Relative order is explicit; no calendar year is given. Resignation remains undated and is not stretched into a dynasty-long window.

evidence.quote: 後為黃門侍郎，棄官東歸

itemChecks.event: Wang Xianzhi fell ill shortly after Xie An died and then died in office.
itemChecks.reason: Owner is Wang Xianzhi (p082). s0345 及安薨 is Xie An’s death, then s0292 未幾，獻之遇疾 and s0295 俄而卒於官; the Huizhi bio independently has s0239 未幾，獻之卒. The dated event is Xianzhi’s own death, not the later honors debate as living activity. Jin Shu Xiaowu annals date 安薨 to 東晉孝武帝太元十年八月丁酉 (not Sun Wu 太元). Calendar tables place 太元十年八月朔 丙子 on AD 385-09-21 Julian, so 丁酉 is AD 385-10-12 Julian; proleptic Gregorian stays AD 385 and is not a New-Year-edge case. 未幾／俄而 after mid-autumn 385 is uncertain within late 385 or 386; onOrAfter 385 and onOrBefore 386 describe that uncertainty and do not invent an exact year.

itemChecks.event: Wang Huizhi died a little over a month after Wang Xianzhi when an old back abscess burst.
itemChecks.reason: Owner is Wang Huizhi (p083). s0241 月餘亦卒 follows s0239 獻之卒 and names Huizhi’s own death, cause 先有背疾，遂潰裂. Because Xianzhi died on or after Xie An’s AD 385 death, Huizhi’s death is onOrAfter 385 (still possible in 385). No upper year is stated, and 月餘 after a 385–386 death could reach 386 or early 387; leaving a one-sided bound does not invent a second endpoint.

evidence.quote: 先有背疾，遂潰裂，月餘亦卒

itemChecks.event: Wang Xianzhi is attested in the sequence from Xie An’s death to Xianzhi’s own death soon afterward.
itemChecks.reason: Owner is Wang Xianzhi (p082). The same 及安薨……未幾，獻之卒 chain as claim-663 dates Xianzhi’s own last illness and death, not a reception of him. The AD 385–386 bounds follow Xie An’s 太元十年八月丁酉 death (AD 385) plus 未幾／俄而. s0235 與獻之俱病篤 is the shared illness in that sequence, not an independent year.

itemChecks.event: Wang Huizhi’s Palace Attendant tenure, eastern return, shared illness, and death are told in relative order without a year in these sentences.
itemChecks.reason: Owner is Wang Huizhi (p083). s0235–s0241 give 後為／棄官／俱病篤／月餘亦卒 with no reign year. Treating this run as an undated attestation, while the separate death claim keeps the Xie An-derived bound, does not invent a year from 後為 or turn the sequence into dynasty-long activity.

evidence.quote: 後為黃門侍郎，棄官東歸，與獻之俱病篤

itemChecks.event: Wang Huizhi fell critically ill together with Wang Xianzhi after leaving office.
itemChecks.reason: Owner is Wang Huizhi (p083). s0235 與獻之俱病篤 is his own illness. This sentence has no year. Dating belongs on Xianzhi’s parallel 未幾，獻之遇疾 after 安薨 and on Huizhi’s later death; leaving this clause undated does not invent a year or use a reception date as activity.

evidence.quote: 棄官東歸，與獻之俱病篤

itemChecks.event: Wang Xianzhi fell critically ill shortly after Xie An died.
itemChecks.reason: Owner is Wang Xianzhi (p082). s0235 與獻之俱病篤 is the same crisis as s0292 未幾，獻之遇疾 after s0345 及安薨. The illness is Xianzhi’s own. Western bounds onOrAfter 385 and onOrBefore 386 rest on Xie An’s 太元十年八月丁酉 death in AD 385 plus 未幾, not on a reign-year-only label treated as a Gregorian day.

itemChecks.event: Zuo Si’s Zhaoyin poems were recited by Wang Huizhi; this is later reception, not Zuo Si’s own dated activity.
itemChecks.reason: Owner of the dated-activity question is Zuo Si (p077), but s0229 詠左思《招隱詩》 is Huizhi reciting an already-written work. Retrospective-reference is the correct kind. The reception’s own scene is undated and must not feed a life date or active hint for Zuo Si.

itemChecks.event: Jing Dan was praised for purity in the brothers’ night reading; this is later reception, not Jing Dan’s own activity.
itemChecks.reason: Owner of the reception is Jing Dan (p080). s0232 獻之賞井丹高潔 is Xianzhi praising a Gao Shi Zhuan exemplar. kind retrospective-reference / receptionType retrospective is required. No calendar year, and no life date for Jing Dan, is supported.

itemChecks.event: Sima Xiangru was cited as scorning the world in Huizhi’s reply; this is later reception, not Xiangru’s own activity.
itemChecks.reason: Owner of the reception is Sima Xiangru (p081), named as 長卿. s0232 未若長卿慢世也 is Huizhi’s comparison during the undated reading. Retrospective classification is correct. The reply’s date is not Xiangru’s life date or activity.

itemChecks.event: The empty hint lists no dated personal event for Zuo Si.
itemChecks.reason: Zuo Si appears only as the author recited in s0229. That is retrospective reception, not a supported personal activity date. Empty active hints are required.

itemChecks.event: The empty hint lists no dated personal event for Dai Kui.
itemChecks.reason: Dai Kui’s only owned event is undated 逵時在剡. No reign year supports an active-date hint. Empty hints match the undated attestation and place claim.

itemChecks.event: The empty hint lists no dated personal event for Wang Xianzhi in the night-reading scene.
itemChecks.reason: p079 is attested only in the undated 嘗夜 reading. Xianzhi’s death bounds belong to p082 and must not be copied here as activity. Empty hints are correct for this person id.

itemChecks.event: The empty hint lists no dated personal event for Jing Dan.
itemChecks.reason: Jing Dan is only praised as an exemplar. Reception must not become an active hint. Empty hints are required.

itemChecks.event: The empty hint lists no dated personal event for Sima Xiangru.
itemChecks.reason: Xiangru is only compared as 長卿. That later reference is not living activity. Empty hints are required.

itemChecks.event: Wang Huizhi died a little over a month after Wang Xianzhi.
itemChecks.reason: The hint restates Huizhi’s death (s0241 月餘亦卒 after 獻之卒), which is a life-date event already carried by claim-664. Active-date-hints must track supported personal activity, not birth or death. His Palace Attendant tenure, resignation, and 俱病篤 illness remain undated in the Chinese. Using the death as an active hint mixes death with activity.

personChecks.reason: Zuo Si has no birth, death, or age in the owned units. The only appearance is Huizhi reciting 《招隱詩》, already classified as retrospective. Empty hints and the reception claim are coherent; no omitted life date exists to add.
Dai Kui is present in Shan in an undated anecdote. No birth, death, or age is stated. Attestation and place-association remain undated; empty hints match. 子楨之 in s0242 is Huizhi’s son, not Dai Kui.

This person id owns only the undated night reading with Huizhi. No age or birth appears. Death and the Xie An sequence are claimed on p082, not here. Empty hints avoid treating later death dates as p079 activity.

personChecks.reason: Jing Dan has no biographical dates in these units. The praise is later reception. Empty hints and the retrospective claim are complete for the supplied evidence.
Sima Xiangru has no biographical dates here. 長卿慢世 is Huizhi’s comparison, already marked retrospective. Empty hints are required.

Huizhi’s own death 月餘亦卒 after 獻之卒 is supported as onOrAfter AD 385 from Xie An’s 太元十年八月 death; office and 俱病篤 stay undated in these sentences; s0242 names a son but gives no birth or age. Chronology is incoherent because hints-p083 uses that death as an active-date hint. Death must remain on the death claim and off activity hints.

findings.problem: hints-p083 uses Wang Huizhi’s death a month after Xianzhi as an active-date hint, mixing a life-date death with personal activity.
findings.action: Replace hints-p083 with an empty active-hint array. Keep claim-664 as the death record with onOrAfter AD 385; do not turn the death into activity or invent office/illness years.
